Palliative Intra-Arterial Chemotherapy Without Radiotherapy for Elderly Patients 
With Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: A Single-Center Retrospective Comparison 
With Radical Cystectomy and Best Supportive Care.

Kusano S(1), Tobu S(1), Yukimoto M(1), Yamaguchi Y(1), Maeda A(1), Kakinoki 
Y(1), Kakinoki H(1), Kawasaki M(1), Yamaguchi K(2), Egashira Y(2), Noguchi M(1).

Author information:
(1)Department of Urology, Faculty of Medicine, Saga University, Saga, Japan.
(2)Department of Radiology, Faculty of Medicine, Saga University, Saga, Japan.

BACKGROUND: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) in elderly patients poses a 
significant treatment challenge owing to the high invasiveness of radical 
cystectomy (RC) and limited tolerability of systemic therapies. Intra-arterial 
chemotherapy (IAC), traditionally used in combination with radiotherapy, has 
shown potential as a local tumor control strategy. However, evidence of its use 
without concurrent radiation remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the clinical efficacy of palliative IAC (P-IAC) 
without radiotherapy in elderly patients with MIBC and compared outcomes between 
RC and best supportive care (BSC).
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 137 patients ≥ 70 years old with MIBC 
who were treated at a single institution between 2010 and 2025. The patients 
were categorized into three groups: P-IAC (n = 43), RC (n = 51), and BSC 
(n = 43). Outcomes included the overall survival (OS), symptom-free survival 
(SFS), and treatment-related adverse events.
RESULTS: The P-IAC group demonstrated a significantly longer SFS (p < 0.001) and 
OS (p = 0.01) compared with the BSC group and no statistically significant 
difference in OS compared with the RC group (p = 0.08). Notably, approximately 
67% of patients with P-IAC remained free of major clinical events at 60 months
